unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of Fe-7Al-0.5C (Table IV): Al 6.95, Si 0.15, Mn 0.12, S 0.004, C 0.50 wt.%.
Table V caption labels the carbon-series route 'AIM', but the section text (b0060) states these alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (AIMFC).
Precipitation hardening by hard Fe3AlC0.5 is reported as the predominant strengthening mechanism in the carbon-series alloys (b0062).

The paper (b0062) states carbon addition to Fe-7 wt.% Al improved room-temperature strength (396-610 MPa) and decreased elongation (18-3%); these summary ranges are not consistent with the tabulated Table V values for the individual carbon-series alloys and were not used as sample property values.
The largest strength jump in the carbon series occurs between Fe-7Al-0.35C and Fe-7Al-0.5C (UTS 515→928 MPa, YS 480→652 MPa), while total elongation drops from 13% to 8% (Table V).
